hyps.why: Adding a conv on the direct input-to-output edge when it was absent restores a strong path, whereas replacing an existing op gives small gains.
With the direct 0->3 edge absent, removing edge 5 can cut the last path to the output and collapse accuracy.
Replacing a 3x3 conv with a parameter-free skip loses capacity, unlike replacing a weaker op.
Adding a skip where the direct edge was absent reconnects input to output, which helps more than swapping one existing op for another.
Upgrading an identity edge to a 3x3 conv consistently adds useful capacity on all datasets.
Downgrading a 3x3 conv to a 1x1 conv shrinks the receptive field and hurts, while replacing a weak op with a conv helps.
Swapping the final-edge 3x3 conv for identity removes learned capacity, whereas replacing a none/weak op is neutral.
If edge 4 is already absent, dropping edge 5 removes a main route into the output node and causes a large drop.
Pooling in place of a weak 1x1 conv on the direct edge helps, while replacing a 3x3 conv with pooling is roughly neutral.
Replacing a 3x3 conv with identity on edge 4 loses capacity, while adding a skip where edge 4 was absent adds a path.
